# andys_functions.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/references/andys_functions.py`*

Legacy/reference ray propagation utilities.

This file is not the active rayTEM framework API. It predates the current
`Element` / `MicroscopeSection` / `Microscope` model and propagates rays through
parallel arrays `(Z, X, Y, A, B, E)` using methods named `propogate` (typo in the
source). Treat it as reference material for older fitting/calibration ideas, not
as code to import from framework modules.

Current framework code should use `rayTEM.elements` and `rayTEM.assemblies`,
where rays are `(N, 8)` arrays and transfer matrices are expanded with
`fix_mat_dims()`.

---

## Module-level functions

### `plotit(Z, X, Y, A, B, elems)` *(line 222)*
Plots propagated X/Y traces and annotates legacy element spans. It understands
legacy `kind` strings such as `prism`, `sole`, `lens`, `quad`, and `name`.

### `propogate2D(elems, X0, Y0, A0, B0, E0)` *(line 302)*
Allocates six `(steps, nrays)` arrays, seeds row zero from initial coordinates,
then calls each element's `propogate(...)` method in sequence. This is separate
from current `Element.propagate_ray`.

### `update_elems(elems_ext, variables, namesof)` *(line 327)*
Copies a legacy element list and substitutes string-valued `length`/`strength`
fields from optimization variables. It also defines `-name` as the negative of
each variable for quick symmetric fitting.

### `obj_fun(variables, elems_ext, namesof, X0, Y0, A0, B0, E0)` *(line 356)*
Hard-coded objective function for a specific legacy optical setup. It calls
`update_elems` and `propogate2D`, then evaluates selected ray positions at fixed
step indices.

## multipole *(class · line 9)*
Legacy base container for old multipole-like elements.

| Method | Kind | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `multipole.__init__(self, kind, name, length, strength, label)` | method | — |

Stores `kind`, `name`, `length`, `strength`, and `label`. Subclasses implement
`propogate` by mutating the next row in the six propagation arrays.

### `multipole.__init__(self, kind, name, length, strength, label)` *(line 10)*
Simple attribute initializer. `__copy__` recreates the same class with copied
name/length/strength/label.

## quad *(class · line 23)*
Legacy quadrupole element.

| Method | Kind | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `quad.__init__(self, name, length, strength, label)` | method | — |
| `quad.propogate(self, Z, X, Y, A, B, E, step)` | method | — |

Uses trigonometric/hyperbolic transfer equations depending on the sign of
`strength`; zero strength falls back to drift behavior.

### `quad.__init__(self, name, length, strength, label)` *(line 24)*
Initializes a legacy element with `kind='quad'`.

### `quad.propogate(self, Z, X, Y, A, B, E, step)` *(line 26)*
Writes row `step + 1` from row `step` for X/Y positions and angles. Energy is
copied through unchanged.

## lens *(class · line 76)*
Legacy thin lens.

| Method | Kind | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `lens.__init__(self, name, length, strength, label)` | method | — |
| `lens.propogate(self, Z, X, Y, A, B, E, step)` | method | — |

Interprets `strength` as focal length after `abs(strength)`. Position and Z do
not advance; angles are kicked by position/focal length.

### `lens.__init__(self, name, length, strength, label)` *(line 77)*
Initializes a legacy element with `kind='lens'`.

### `lens.propogate(self, Z, X, Y, A, B, E, step)` *(line 79)*
Applies `A -= X/f` and `B -= Y/f` when focal length is nonzero.
